features.heading: SMS campaign software for the whole messaging workflow
features.intro: IEOSUIA SMS Portal brings business SMS preparation, contact groups, prepaid credits and delivery reporting into one workspace for South African messaging operations.

sections.heading: Build an audience before you write
paragraphs: Import Excel or CSV contacts, map their columns and organise them into groups. A group is a saved contact collection; a campaign audience is the selection for one send. Removing someone from a campaign does not delete their contact or group membership.

The campaign review excludes duplicate numbers and opted-out recipients. Check the final sendable audience rather than the original spreadsheet row count. Keep evidence that you may contact the people on your list; software does not provide consent on your behalf.

sections.heading: Compose, personalise and review
paragraphs: Write an SMS or choose a saved template, then edit it for this campaign. Use supported editor variables and ensure the recipient fields are populated. Review the opt-out footer choice before calculating the message requirement.

Personalisation, Unicode and longer text can increase billable segments. The server-calculated campaign preview is the authoritative requirement. Remove recipients or fit the audience to available credits without deleting contacts.

sections.heading: Choose dispatch timing and follow the outcome
paragraphs: Send immediately or schedule a later date and time. Completed dispatch means the campaign has finished its submission work, not that every handset has confirmed delivery.

Campaign details and Reports show recipient-level outcomes and offer exports. An unavailable delivery report is not a confirmed failure. Review the linked delivery guide before deciding whether to retry.

sections.heading: Available in this release
paragraphs: SMS campaigns, contacts and groups, SMS templates, scheduling, delivery reports, exports and prepaid credits are available. Email Campaigns are Coming Soon.

This release does not promise email sending, A/B testing, click tracking, geographical analytics or recommended send times. Check the workflow guides to decide whether the current product meets your needs.

use-cases.heading: Practical business SMS uses in South Africa
use-cases.intro: Start with a defined audience and a clear reason to contact it. These are examples of workflows using the portal's existing groups, templates and scheduling, not automated integrations or claims about existing customers.

sections.heading: Retail promotions and customer updates
paragraphs: Prepare a short promotion for customers who may receive your updates. Include an accurate offer date, relevant store information and an appropriate opt-out instruction. Check the final segment count before sending.
Do not assume an old customer record permits every marketing message. Keep promotion groups distinct from essential service-update audiences and review exclusions before each campaign.

sections.heading: Schools, churches and communities
paragraphs: Schools can group parent or guardian contacts for timetable changes and event reminders. Churches and community organisations can prepare meeting notices for their own contact groups. Check the correct group carefully before dispatch.

Avoid sensitive personal details in bulk messages. Direct a recipient to an appropriate private channel when needed. Network delays are possible, so SMS should not be the only channel for safety-critical notices.

sections.heading: Events and internal teams
paragraphs: Prepare event reminders in advance, check the venue and time, then schedule the campaign. If the event changes, check the original campaign status before sending a correction.

Use separate groups for shift reminders or operational notices. Templates reduce repeated typing, but dates and locations still need review. Scheduling sets dispatch timing rather than guaranteeing the exact time a handset receives the message.

sections.heading: Service reminders and collection notices
paragraphs: Select relevant contacts for a service reminder, collection notice or order update. These examples require your campaign preparation; they do not imply an automatic connection to an order or booking system.

After sending, review recipient outcomes. Investigate a confirmed failure before retrying, and do not resend all pending messages because confirmation is delayed. Keep recipient data private when sharing exports with a team.

contact-management.heading: Prepare contacts and groups for SMS campaigns
contact-management.intro: Build a clean audience using Excel .xlsx or CSV imports, saved contact groups and campaign-specific recipient selection. Start with a small test file before importing your full list.

sections.heading: Prepare the file and mapping
paragraphs: Use a header row such as Name, Phone and Email, with one recipient per row. Store phone numbers as text so spreadsheet software does not remove a leading zero or convert them to scientific notation. Review numbers before upload.

Choose the relevant Excel worksheet. Match each portal field to the correct spreadsheet column and select an existing group when appropriate. Understandable column names help, but do not replace reviewing the mapping.

sections.heading: Check what was imported
paragraphs: Review imported, duplicate and rejected counts. The number of new contacts can be lower than the file row count when duplicates are present. Correct invalid entries rather than repeatedly importing the same file.

Open several imported records and confirm their names, numbers and email fields. Verify the intended group allocation. Keep the source file secure and only upload information you are authorised to use.

sections.heading: Separate saved contacts from sendable recipients
paragraphs: Select a group or individual recipients for a campaign. The final preview excludes duplicate numbers and opted-out contacts. If credits are insufficient, remove recipients or fit the campaign to available credits.

Those campaign exclusions do not delete the saved contacts or group membership. Recalculate after changing audience or message content; personalisation and footer text may affect the required segments.

sections.heading: Respect opt-outs and privacy
paragraphs: Review the Opted Out view and do not re-import a person to work around suppression. If a request appears unprocessed, provide support with the relevant campaign reference rather than a full contact export.
Contact features support your responsibilities but are not a legal certification or guarantee of POPIA compliance. Read the privacy and POPIA information and seek appropriate advice for your use.

scheduled-sms.heading: Schedule SMS campaigns with a clear review process
scheduled-sms.intro: Prepare a campaign ahead of time and select a later dispatch date. Scheduling helps organise reminders, but recipients, message content, credits and delivery outcomes still need review.

sections.heading: Before choosing the time
paragraphs: Choose the audience, compose the message and review personalisation and the opt-out footer. Calculate the final requirement after all changes. Longer text or Unicode may increase the segments per recipient.
Check the date and time shown in the review. If your device is set to a different timezone, confirm the intended South African dispatch time rather than assuming the device clock matches it.

sections.heading: Dispatch is not handset delivery
paragraphs: The scheduled time indicates when the system should begin dispatching an eligible campaign. Provider acceptance, network routing and handset availability occur after that. An exact arrival-time guarantee would be misleading.
The portal provides manual scheduling, not automatic recommendations for an optimal marketing hour. Choose a time appropriate to recipient expectations and leave margin for time-sensitive reminders.

sections.heading: After the scheduled time
paragraphs: Check whether dispatch has started and whether individual messages were submitted. Then review the delivery states. Completed dispatch can still include messages waiting for final delivery confirmation.

If a campaign has not progressed, record its reference, selected time and displayed status for support. Avoid creating another copy until you know whether the original was submitted. This helps prevent duplicate messages and charges.

delivery-reports.heading: Understand SMS delivery reports and recipient status
delivery-reports.intro: Sending and delivery are different events. The portal records campaign activity and individual outcomes; final delivery confirmation depends on the SMS provider. Use status and details together, not a campaign total alone.

sections.heading: Read the status correctly
paragraphs: Sent means the provider accepted the message for sending. Delivered requires a delivery confirmation. Failed or undelivered represents a reported unsuccessful outcome, not merely a missing delivery report.

Pending includes messages without final confirmation. Confirmation unavailable means a delivery-report lookup has not supplied an outcome. The recipient may have received the message, so this is not proof of failure or an instruction to resend.

sections.heading: Compare the right records and period
paragraphs: Open a campaign to inspect recipient numbers, segment counts, timestamps and available provider details. Match the reporting period when comparing Dashboard, Reports and campaign history. Totals from different ranges are not directly comparable.

Delivery percentages count messages; credit usage counts billable segments. Three recipients with two segments each produce three message records and consume six credits, not six delivered recipients.

sections.heading: Export and share carefully
paragraphs: Use CSV, Excel or PDF exports for the campaign or report you are reviewing. Retain the reporting period and campaign reference so another person can reconcile the figures. Share recipient information only with authorised people.
Delivery reports do not prove that someone read an SMS or clicked a link. Engagement, device and geographical analytics are not promised by this release.

sections.heading: Investigate before retrying
paragraphs: Inspect the recipient number and provider details for a confirmed failure. If a report is unavailable, ask support to investigate the reference instead of resending the entire campaign.

Provide the campaign reference, reporting period and displayed status. Do not share passwords, card details or the full contact list. This gives support evidence without exposing unnecessary personal information.
